name: Amendments to the Constitution of Ireland (1937–2024)
title: Amendments to the Constitution of Ireland (1937–2024)
description: Every proposed amendment to Bunreacht na hÉireann with its subject, enactment date, referendum date, electorate, turnout, votes for and against, and a short description of the change.

rows.subject: Adoption of the Constitution
rows.description: The draft Constitution was not a bill, but was passed by Dáil Éireann in the same manner as a bill before it was submitted for approval by the electorate.

rows.subject: Definition of war
rows.description: Extended the definition of "time of war" to include a war in which the state is not a participant. This was to allow the Government to exercise emergency powers during the Second World War, in which the state was neutral.

rows.subject: Textual adjustments
rows.description: An omnibus bill with a variety of mostly minor textual amendments. Some changes were only to the Irish text, to correspond more closely to the sense of the English text.

rows.subject: Elections: Dáil: electoral system
rows.description: Proposal to alter the electoral system for elections to Dáil Éireann from the multi-member single transferable vote (STV) to the single-member First Past the Post (FPTP) system. It also proposed to establish an independent commission for boundary delimitation of Dáil constituencies.

rows.subject: Elections: Dáil: constituency boundaries
rows.description: Proposed to allow greater malapportionment in favour of rural areas in boundary delimitation of Dáil constituencies.

rows.subject: Elections: Dáil: electoral system
rows.description: A second proposal to alter the Dáil electoral system from STV to FPTP.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Accession
rows.description: Permitted the state to join the European Communities.

rows.subject: Elections: franchise: voting age
rows.description: Reduced the minimum voting age from 21 to 18.

rows.subject: Recognition of religions
rows.description: Removed reference to the "special position" of the Catholic Church and to other named denominations.

rows.subject: Adoption board
rows.description: Reversed a 1977 finding that certain orders made by the adoption board were unconstitutional.

rows.subject: Seanad: university constituencies
rows.description: Allowed the Seanad representation of Dublin University and the National University to be extended to graduates of other third-level institutions. This provision was not invoked until 2024, with the Seanad Electoral (University Members) (Amendment) Bill 2024.

rows.subject: Abortion: recognised the equal right to life of the unborn
rows.description: Gave constitutional recognition to the equal right to life of the unborn to entrench the statutory prohibition of abortion. Repealed on 18 September 2018, upon enactment of the 36th Amendment.

rows.subject: Elections: franchise: votes for non-citizens
rows.description: Permitted legislation to be enacted allowing citizens of other countries to vote in elections for Dáil Éireann.

rows.subject: Rights: Divorce
rows.description: Proposed to remove the constitutional ban on divorce. The ban was eventually lifted by the Fifteenth Amendment in 1996.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Single European Act
rows.description: Permitted the state to ratify the Single European Act.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Maastricht Treaty
rows.description: Permitted the state to ratify the Maastricht Treaty (the Treaty on European Union).

rows.subject: Abortion: exclusion of suicide
rows.description: Proposed to specify that a pregnancy may be terminated in the case of a real and substantial risk of life to the mother, but not in the case of a risk of suicide. This would have reversed part of the 1992 Supreme Court judgment in the X Case, which had held that abortion was permissible in the case of a risk of suicide.

rows.subject: Abortion: right to travel
rows.description: Specified that the prohibition of abortion would not limit freedom of travel in and out of the state. Repealed on 18 September 2018, upon enactment of the 36th Amendment.

rows.subject: Abortion: right to information
rows.description: Specified that the prohibition of abortion would not limit the right to distribute information about abortion services in foreign countries. Repealed on 18 September 2018, upon enactment of the 36th Amendment.

rows.subject: Rights: Divorce
rows.description: Removed the constitutional ban on divorce, but retained certain restrictions on its occurrence.

rows.subject: Rights: bail restrictions
rows.description: Permitted a court to refuse someone bail if it suspected they would commit a serious criminal offence while at liberty. This reversed a 1965 Supreme Court ruling.

rows.subject: Cabinet confidentiality
rows.description: To reverse a 1992 Supreme Court ruling that meetings of the cabinet were absolutely confidential, and to permit the High Court to order the disclosure of cabinet discussions in certain circumstances.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Treaty of Amsterdam
rows.description: Allowed the state to ratify the Treaty of Amsterdam.

rows.subject: Treaty: Good Friday Agreement
rows.description: Allowed the state to be bound by the Good Friday Agreement and provided for the conditional amendment of Articles 2 and 3 of the Constitution, which subsequently came into effect on the implementation of the Good Friday Agreement.

rows.subject: Elections: Local government
rows.description: Provided that local government elections must occur every five years.

rows.subject: Rights: Death penalty
rows.description: Introduced a constitutional ban on legislation for capital punishment, even in a time of national emergency.

rows.subject: Courts: judges: discipline
rows.description: Proposed to establish a body for the investigation of judges and to amend the procedure for the removal of judges. It was introduced to the Oireachtas but lapsed after its second stage.

rows.subject: Treaty: Rome Statute of the ICC
rows.description: Allowed the state to ratify the Statute of the International Criminal Court.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Treaty of Nice
rows.description: Proposed to allow the state to ratify the Treaty of Nice. Voters reversed this decision when they adopted the Twenty-sixth Amendment in 2002.

rows.subject: Abortion: exclusion of suicide
rows.description: This was a second attempt to strengthen the constitutional ban on abortion and to prevent risk of suicide being invoked as grounds for an abortion.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Treaty of Nice
rows.description: Allowed the state to ratify the Nice Treaty.

rows.subject: Irish nationality
rows.description: Abolished constitutional jus soli right to Irish nationality.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Treaty of Lisbon
rows.description: Proposed to allow the state to ratify the Treaty of Lisbon. Voters reversed this decision when they adopted the Twenty-eighth Amendment in 2009.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: Treaty of Lisbon
rows.description: Allowed the state to ratify the Treaty of Lisbon.

rows.subject: Courts: judges: remuneration
rows.description: Relaxed the prohibition on the reduction of the salaries of Irish judges.

rows.subject: Oireachtas inquiries
rows.description: Proposed to reverse a 2002 Supreme Court ruling which prevented Oireachtas inquiries from making findings critical of individuals called to give evidence.

rows.subject: Treaty: Europe: European Fiscal Compact
rows.description: Allowed the state to ratify the European Fiscal Compact.

rows.subject: Rights: Children
rows.description: A general statement of children's rights, and a provision intended to secure the power of the state to take children into care who are at risk of abuse or neglect from their parents.

rows.subject: Seanad: abolition
rows.description: Proposed to abolish Seanad Éireann.

rows.subject: Courts: new Court of Appeal
rows.description: Mandates a new Court of Appeal above the High Court and below the Supreme Court.

rows.subject: Rights: Same-sex marriage
rows.description: Prohibits restriction on civil marriage based on sex (civil partnership had been established under a 2010 statute).

rows.subject: Presidency: reduce age of candidacy to 21.
rows.description: Proposed to lower the minimum age for the presidency from 35 to 21.

rows.subject: Abortion: Repeal of the 8th Amendment
rows.description: Removed clauses added by the 8th, 13th, and 14th Amendments of the Constitution and allowed the Oireachtas to legislate for the regulation of termination of pregnancy.

rows.subject: Blasphemy
rows.description: Removed the offence of publication or utterance of blasphemous matter from the Constitution.

rows.subject: Rights: Divorce
rows.description: Removed the requirement of a period of separation before proceedings for divorce are initiated, and allowed for recognition of foreign divorces.

rows.subject: Family: Non-marital relationships
rows.description: Proposal to expand recognition of the family to include durable relationships.

rows.subject: Family: Care
rows.description: Proposal to remove reference to woman's life within the home and mothers' duties in the home, and to insert new provision on care within the family.
